ground_truth.unit: logit coefficient per real dollar of sugar-industry contributions
ground_truth.location: Table 1, District fixed effects, Inflation-adjusted sugar contributions
ground_truth.context: Table 1 ("The Determinants of Voting in Favor of Sugar Reform"), column District fixed effects, row Inflation-adjusted sugar contributions.  Logit; the dependent variable equals 1 for "aye" votes on the two reform amendments to the U.S. sugar program (the 2013 Pitts amendment, H. Amdt. 227 to H.R. 1947, and the 2018 Foxx amendment, H. Amdt. 605 to H.R. 2; aye = a vote against sugar interests) and 0 otherwise.  One observation per House district and vote; the two votes are treated as repeated votes on the same issue. Regressor: inflation-adjusted sugar-industry contributions (all sugar-industry PACs plus individual contributions over $200 from people working in the sugar industry, Center for Responsive Politics) to the incumbent, aggregated from one year before the vote through the end of the calendar year of the vote.  Controls: the American Conservative Union ideology score (ACU, 1-100, higher = more conservative), tenure, the district poverty rate, % with a bachelor's degree, median income, % population over 65, and a dummy for membership on the House agriculture committee.  District fixed effects, so only the districts whose vote outcome changed between the two amendments identify the coefficients.  Probability values from robust standard errors; the table prints coefficient (p), p = 0.001, significant at 1%.

i4r.notes: DP 57 Table 1 col 1 (robust SEs reproduction), -0.0006, p < 0.001.

Robust standard errors; the table prints p = 0.001, significant at 1%.

i4r.notes: DP 57 Table 1 col 2, -0.0004, p < 0.001 (the meta-database row's r_coeff "-.004" is a slip).

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: Inflation adjustment: the paper does not give its deflator; contributions (totalcont) are converted to 2018 dollars with CPI-U annual averages (2013 = 232.957, 2018 = 251.107), using the vote year's CPI for every window.

Window-to-file mapping inferred from the data: SugarReplicate.dta = baseline window (largest totals, nests the others); SugarReplicate_iter2.dta = calendar year of the vote (larger 2018 total, smaller 2013 total, consistent with the fall-2012 and fall-2018 election-season giving); SugarReplicate_iter1.dta = 12 months before the vote. The variable sugcont is identical across files and is not used (taken to be the cycle-aggregated measure of the paper's Appendix A.3).

Fixed-effects logit estimated as unconditional ML with fixed-effect dummies (fixest::feglm, binomial), which drops districts or incumbents whose vote did not change; heteroskedasticity-robust SEs. ACU score is the data's ncu variable.
deviations_stdout: inflation adjustment uses CPI-U annual averages (2013=232.957, 2018=251.107), contributions in 2018 dollars; the paper does not state its deflator.
window-to-file mapping (iter2=calendar year, iter1=12 months) inferred from election-year timing of contribution totals.
cell.notes: Outcome y = 1 if vote == 'Aye', 0 otherwise (No, Not Voting, No Vote). Controls: ACU (ncu), tenure, poverty, bach, medincome, over65, agcom; fixed effects on the district id (state_no*100 + district). Rows with missing covariates dropped (2 rows), leaving 93 vote-switching districts (186 obs), matching the paper's 93. Incumbent sample: districts where both rows have both == 1 (same member cast both votes); 53 switching incumbents (106 obs), matching the paper's 53; FE on district id, which equals incumbent FE in this sample (one switching pair has inconsistent cid codes across the two congresses, so grouping by cid would give 52). Three exploratory runs (attempt-1..3, no RESULT lines) inspected variables, contribution totals by file and switching counts; the replication Read Me (.docx) was read as data documentation. No script files in the package were opened. All work ran from the scratch dir <scratch>/.../cells/grier-blind-4 and was copied here.
